profiled_workloads.selection_reason: Lowest eval speedup (0.150) and highest eval latency (1.715 ms) in the round; representative of the three dim=-1 large [1024,4096] cases (timing-1/4/7) that dominate the geo_mean.

Largest latency improvement from the round-3 constexpr-INNER change (-33.6%); representative of the strided dim=0 regime (inner=128) and of the boundary where the regression being fixed actually responded.
Strong control: same geometry as timing-2 but bfloat16 and the only workload above 1x (1.876x), used to separate dtype effects from geometry effects in the strided regime.
Smallest shape of the contiguous dim=-1 family (128x1024, 128 programs); isolates the small-latency regime where eval walltime exceeds the device task and launch cost can matter.
Third dtype of the strided regime (float32, inner=128); gives a dtype-independent boundary reading of the mixed scalar/MTE2 regime.

findings.label: Contiguous (inner==1) rays are saturated on the AIV Scalar pipe by a per-element scan recurrence, with Vector and both MTE pipes idle
findings.inference: For the dim=-1 geometry the kernel issues 1024 (timing-1) or 128 (timing-0) programs, each walking the scan axis serially, and the AIV Scalar pipe accounts for 98.5% / 95.7% of AIV time while Vector is 0.6% / 0.9%. The cost is proportional to the number of scan steps, not to stride or dtype: 0.40 ns per scanned element for timing-1 (4.19 M steps) versus 0.505 ns per scanned element for timing-0 (0.13 M steps), and the identical 0.505 ns/element for the strided timing-2/5/8 at the same 128x1023 step count. Since stride differs by 128x between those groups while the per-step scalar cost does not, the scalar work is the sequential accumulation of the prefix itself (the tl.cumsum over the 1023/4095-long axis at source line 53), not address arithmetic. Scalar is therefore the throughput limit on these cases, and splitting rays across more programs cannot help because the total number of scan steps is fixed by the output element count.

findings.label: The contiguous ray is already moved by block DMA; memory is off the critical path for the 1.715 ms cases

evidence.unit: us (mte3 5.987 us) against avg duration 1711.037 us

findings.inference: Each invocation moves 1024*4096 fp16 in and 1024*4095 fp16 out (16.8 MB) while MTE2+MTE3 busy time totals about 16.7 us, under 1% of the 1711 us task. The interface rate implied by that (about 1.5 TB/s) is only reachable because the 176 MB L2 holds this working set across the 100 repeated invocations, so this is an interface counter and not an HBM-physical-bandwidth statement; either way DMA granularity and bandwidth cannot explain the 6.7x gap to the 0.257 ms reference. It also confirms that the constexpr-INNER rewrite did produce block DMA for the stride-1 ray, which is the addressing mechanism the frozen hypothesis predicted.

findings.label: Strided (inner=128, dim=0) rays alternate between strided transfer and the scan recurrence instead of overlapping them
findings.inference: In the strided regime the marginal pipe ratios sum to about 1.02 (timing-2), 1.00 (timing-8) and 1.01 (timing-5), consistent with the strided GM<->UB transfer and the scalar recurrence being effectively serialized inside each program; only 128 programs exist (about 6.4 waves on the 20 AI cores), so per-block stalls cannot be hidden by other blocks. Scalar remains the single largest pipe but is no longer dominant, so these cases are genuinely mixed. These are marginal active-time fractions, not a time decomposition, and a sum near 1.0 is an observation of serialization rather than a proof of zero overlap.

findings.label: Small contiguous case: eval walltime exceeds the profiled device task by roughly one third

evidence.metric: distinct op rows in the capture (single kernel present)

findings.inference: The authoritative eval latency for timing-0 is 0.1052 ms while the only device task in the capture averages 69.25 us, leaving about 36 us per call that no device task accounts for. Because the two numbers come from different captures they must not be subtracted as an exact host/device split, but the direction is consistent with host-side launch and binding cost being material at this size, and the 69.25 us already contains 66.1 us of scalar scan. timing-1 shows the opposite regime: consecutive task start times in its op_summary are spaced by about the task duration itself, so there is no comparable per-call gap at large size.

findings.label: The round-3 constexpr-INNER change fixed the strided regime only; the scalar-bound contiguous regime was untouched

evidence.unit: cycles per scanned element for the strided dim=0 path (8940661 / (128*1023))

evidence.metric: aiv_scalar_ratio on the unchanged dim=-1 path

findings.inference: The frozen hypothesis for this round was that a compile-time INNER stride would collapse the strided-ray overhead toward the ~15 cycles/element tl.cumsum floor. Authoritative eval numbers show the strided dim=0 cases moving by -33.6% (timing-2), -33.5% (timing-5) and -26.1% (timing-8) latency, while the three dim=-1 cases are unchanged (-0.1% to +0.06%), so the hypothesis is supported for the regime it targeted and the mechanism (constant-folded pid arithmetic plus block DMA on the ray) is consistent with the near-zero MTE2 ratio now seen on timing-1. It is not sufficient for the round: the strided cases still cost 68.3 cycles per scanned element and the geo_mean is pinned by timing-1/4/7 at 0.150-0.187.

performance_interpretation: Round 3 is numerically PASSED and the fingerprint is trusted. The geo_mean moved from 0.3535 (round-1 baseline) to 0.4108 (+16.2%), entirely from the dim=0 strided cases, but three workloads (timing-1/4/7, dim=-1 on [1024,4096]) remain at 1.705-1.715 ms and 0.150-0.187 speedup and alone hold the mean down. Profiler facts: the kernel is a single device task per call in every profiled workload; on the contiguous dim=-1 shapes the AIV Scalar pipe carries 95.7-98.5% of AIV time while Vector (0.6-0.9%) and both MTE pipes (0.3-3.5%) are effectively idle, at a stable 0.40-0.505 ns of scalar time per scanned element regardless of stride and dtype. That invariance across a 128x change in stride identifies the serial prefix accumulation at main.py:53 as the limit rather than addressing or bandwidth, and it explains why raising the program count or removing the mask cannot help: the number of scan steps equals the number of output elements. On the strided dim=0 shapes the same scan work consumes an identical scalar span (66.1 us) but the strided transfer now costs 29-36% and the four pipe ratios sum to about 1.0, so those cases are mixed and serialized at only 128 programs. Two distinct regimes coexist, which is why dominant_bound is recorded as mixed rather than compute. Practical calibration: for the identical [128,1024] fp16 scanned element count the frozen reference cumsum device kernel measures 35.9 us in the paired trace while our in-kernel scan needs 66.1 us, so a better scan lowering has roughly 2x of headroom inside one kernel and the fused candidate can still win overall once the scan is no longer scalar-serialized. Profiler timing is diagnostic throughout; the eval walltimes quoted are the only authoritative performance numbers.

next_experiment.action_description: Restructure the scan for every case, not just the strided one: view each program's masked (N-1)-length ray as a 2-D tile of shape (S, L) with L=64 and S=BLOCK/L, compute the local cumsum of the increments along the L axis, take each segment's total, compute the exclusive prefix over the S segment totals with one short cumsum, and broadcast-add it back. Keep the fp32 promote, the (a+b)*0.5 scale, the same output-dtype conversion and the existing tail mask, and zero the padded lanes so they cannot contaminate segment totals. Do not add kernels, temporary GM buffers or host work, and leave the outer/inner grid mapping and program count unchanged.
next_experiment.expected_impact: Profiler evidence supports the frozen round-3 hypothesis for the regime it targeted and contradicts it as a global fix: making INNER constexpr removed the strided-ray penalty (timing-2/5/8 latency -26% to -34%) but the contiguous cases carrying 98.5% scalar stay at 1.71 ms. If the short-axis cumsum is vectorized across the S independent segments, the dependent step count per program falls from 4095 to about 128 vector steps, so timing-1 should fall from 1711 us toward a few hundred us, with aiv_scalar_ratio dropping well below 0.5 and aiv_vec_ratio rising on the same workload, moving timing-1/4/7 off 0.15-0.19 toward the 0.257 ms reference.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: The association changes from a strict sequential fp32 prefix to a blocked two-level sum, which is a numerical change, and none of the 24 frozen correctness cases exercises a long scan axis, so the 9 timing shapes must be verified numerically at the contract tolerances (fp32 atol/rtol 1e-4 is the sensitive one). 4095 and 1023 are not multiples of 64, so the last segment must be masked with zeros on both the increment and the broadcast-add. If the metric signature does not change (scalar ratio unchanged, vector ratio flat) or any timing input exceeds tolerance, roll back to the current round-3 source (sha f3f72b71) as the working baseline and record the failed variant plus its artifacts rather than tuning tolerances.
success_criteria: Full KGS eval: all 24 correctness workloads PASS with matched_ratio 1.0.

All 9 frozen timing inputs pass an independent numerical check at the contract tolerances (atol/rtol 0.015 for fp16/bf16, 1e-4 for fp32); passing the timing phase alone is not evidence of correctness.
timing-1, timing-4 and timing-7 device time falls below 1.0 ms each (from 1.705-1.715 ms) with eval speedup above 0.40.

metrics on timing-1 show aiv_scalar_ratio dropping well below 0.5 and aiv_vec_ratio rising above 0.10, i.e. the predicted counter change actually occurred; if device time improves without that counter signature, or the signature changes without device time improving, update the hypothesis instead of accepting the result.

msprof device timing is diagnostic and is not eval latency; all speedup and latency statements come from get_profile_context.
The eval timing phase reports PASSED without numeric assertions; the fp32-promotion path of this candidate is not numerically exercised on the 4095-length shapes by the 24 frozen correctness cases.

Pipe ratios are marginal active fractions and must not be summed as a time decomposition; the near-1.0 sums reported for the strided regime are an observation of serialization, not a proof of zero overlap.
open_questions: Is tl.cumsum over a 64-length axis with 64 independent segments actually lowered to vector steps on this FlagTree build, or does it scalarize the same way as the 4095-length axis? This is the decisive unknown for the next experiment and was not resolvable after the instruction capture was cancelled.

Is the ~36 us difference between timing-0's 69.25 us device task and its 0.1052 ms eval walltime attributable to host launch/binding, or does it include other non-kernel work? A launch-only probe with the same ABI would separate it in a single capture.

Which part of the 29-36% MTE2 activity on the strided dim=0 shapes comes from 2-byte-granularity strided access versus unavoidable line traffic? No physical byte counters were collected for those workloads in this round.

The frozen paired trace gives a 35.9 us device cumsum for the same [128,1024] fp16 scanned element count; whether that lowering can be reproduced inside the fused kernel without a second kernel launch remains unverified.
